notes.title: Anomaly Farm is Here!
notes.content: [p]Hello everyone,[/p][p]Today we’re thrilled to release a brand-new way to experience Hired 2 Die: the Anomaly Farm mode![/p][p]This isn’t just a small addition—it’s a completely new way to play. In Anomaly Farm, the rules are twisted, the pressure is higher, and chaos lurks around every corner. Here’s what makes it stand out:[/p][list][*][p]Distortions from both maps, [i]A Simple Job[/i] and [i]The House Always Wins[/i], now appear together in a single, terrifying setting.[/p][/*][*][p]Random modifiers shake up the experience every run—expect the unexpected, from slower movement to limited vision, or facing Distortions under harsher conditions.[/p][/*][*][p]Instead of the usual contracts, this mode is all about a time rush: complete tasks to extend your survival and push your team further.[/p][/*][/list][p]And the best part? Anomaly Farm is available [b]for free[/b] to everyone who already owns the game. No expansions, no extra purchases—just jump in and play.[/p][p]This is only the beginning. We’ll be watching closely as you explore the farm, share your strategies, and discover just how long you can last when everything is against you.[/p][p]See you in the fields. Good luck surviving.[/p][p]— The Hired 2 Die Team[/p]

notes.title: This is not the same game anymore!
notes.content:
[p]Over the past few weeks, we’ve been working non-stop to reshape huge parts of the game based on [b]community feedback[/b], and this latest update might be our biggest one yet.[/p][p] [/p][h2][b]What’s Changed?[/b][/h2][p]
[b]Idferno and Egoshade in “A Simple Job” have been completely rebuilt from scratch.[/b][/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]New AI[/p][/*][*][p]New behaviors[/p][/*][*][p]New materials[/p][/*][*][p]New visual effects[/p][/*][*][p]New sounds[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]They don’t just look different, they play completely differently. Expect new challenges… and maybe new fears.[/p][p] [/p][h2]Massive animation rework across the entire game.[/h2][p] [/p][list][*][p]Cleaning, packing, burning, locking, and dismantling now feel way more fluid, immersive, and satisfying.[/p][/*][*][p]New visual effects and interaction feedback on tasks across all maps.[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h2]New Story Mode.[/h2][p]A much [b]easier game mode[/b] for players who want to enjoy the chaos without sweating too much. Great for learning or casual play. (Look for the little book icon next to START on the contract selection screen!)[/p][p] [/p][h2]It Doesn’t Stop There...[/h2][list][*][p]Cloud Saves now work.[/p][/*][*][p]New map selection screen.[/p][/*][*][p]New accessibility options, including puzzle simplification.[/p][/*][*][p]Shortcut keys for cycling security cameras.[/p][/*][*][p]Tons of gameplay tweaks, balance adjustments, and bug fixes.[/p][/*][*][p]Even the Demo has been updated to reflect all these changes.[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Plus... everything from the last updates:[/p][p]-Portuguese voice acting[/p][p]-Full controller support and official Steam Deck profile[/p][p]-Revamped areas in “A Simple Job” and other maps[/p][p]-Improved character models[/p][p]-Faster task interactions[/p][p]-Faster anomaly photo processing[/p][p]-CPU optimizations[/p][p]-New UI buttons like Back to Main Menu[/p][p] [/p][p]And so much more...[/p][p] [/p][p]Check it out. This might be your first time… [b]or your first time all over again.[/b]
As always, thank you for being part of this community. Your feedback is what keeps Hired 2 Die growing. Let us know what you think![/p][p] [/p][p][url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/1729140"]Click here for the full patch notes[/url] [/p]

notes.title: Devlog #018 | Roadmap Q1
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone,[/b] we are excited to share that we have officially completed the first quarter of our roadmap. As promised, we focused on three major areas for Q1: full controller support, quality of life improvements, and accessibility features.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/cbd909806eae8362829b633e6a18c3852952e746.jpg[/img]
Below, you will find a summary of what has been delivered, along with a brief look at some past patch notes for anyone who might have missed them.

[h1]Full Controller Support[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/42ec38b0447a77b6d4a3732368d88021de4c2532.gif[/img]
[b]You can now fully navigate and play Hired 2 Die using a gamepad:[/b]
We have also added an official Steam Deck controller profile, ensuring smoother gameplay on the device

[h1]Quality of Life Improvements[/h1]

[b]You can see and join rooms from any region, making it easier to find matches and play with friends:[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/a41ea0204b27f4fa1217b10270a0e80f598c9dd9.gif[/img]

[b]We have continued to revamp certain areas of the maps for better visual clarity and narrative cohesion:[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/9b817d741cebc086e42b4b517c591252c4b3f1a4.gif[/img]

As mentioned in earlier patch notes, we improved the visuals of the Control Room and Zone A in "A Simple Job" map.

[h3]Various bug fixes and balancing tweaks have been applied. For example:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed the condition to earn the achievements "Burn in Hell!", "DOWN!", and "Office Party Photos"
[*] Fixed an issue where players could become stuck after dying right when the generator puzzle
[*] We addressed several cases where players might get trapped inside a bathroom stall, the Egoshade cabinet, or other parts of the environment
[*] We removed the first row of lockers in A Simple Job to improve movement in that area
[*] Interaction times for many objectives have been reduced to streamline the overall flow
[*] Magic Eye notices chain sounds from farther away
[*] The difference between Anomalies and Distortions is now clearer when using the anomaly camera
[/list]
[b]The anomaly camera now processes photos faster: [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/7694af4a989af1ee06303ed8e436f8cdecf10964.gif[/img]

[h1]Accessibility Features[/h1]
[b]We have introduced a dedicated Accessibility Menu with multiple categories[/b]:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/b941b9dd702d91919bc9f68ae5d0ac80766de5ba.gif[/img]
[list]
[*] Toggle options for sprinting, crouching, and general actions
[*] Game speed multiplier for solo play
[*] Delay settings for repeated button presses
[*] [b]HUD objective markers:[/b]
[/list] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/452112bf38d217b79842b532e54d817f6470f581.gif[/img]
[list]
[*] Option to remove jumpscares
[*] Sound filters and adjustable blood settings
[*] [b]Colorblindness filters:[/b]
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/847f68757661b53831c1c1c010d84cfe7cc70fd9.gif[/img]
[list] 
[*] Contrast adjustments
[*] Subtitle and Reticle size customization
[*] Speaker names in subtitles
[*] Speech to text and translation settings
[*] Microphone sensitivity adjustments
[*] Forced mute option
[/list]
[h1]And More[/h1]

[b]THIS IS A BIG ONE[/b] 
We have reworked the puddle-cleaning interaction, adding new animations and effects:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/5940a69006368bb403898054cff083fd4668550c.gif[/img]
[list]
[*] We added a new option in the pause menu to leave or close a lobby
[*] Antialiasing quality can now be adjusted
[*] The walkie-talkie voice filter is less harsh
[*] Minor text adjustments have been made in the manual and certain in-game emails to clarify instructions
[*] In previous updates, we also introduced CPU optimizations across multiple stages, improved the female playable character model, added a Back to Main Menu button, and updated the Unity editor version for better stability
[/list]
[h1]LAST BUT NOT LEAST...[/h1]
Steam has officially approved Community Items for Hired 2 Die. That means you can now earn and collect Steam Badges, Trading Cards, Backgrounds, and Emoticons just by playing the game.

There are six different badges to unlock, five unique trading cards to collect and craft, three new profile backgrounds to customize your Steam profile, and five exclusive emoticons to use in chats.

If you've already played Hired 2 Die, you might find that some of these items have already been added to your Steam inventory based on your playtime. So go ahead and check your inventory:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/f341ddd7d7c6f0e0c72bcd2b452328ee5a75c92b.png[/img]

We hope these changes make Hired 2 Die more enjoyable for everyone. Finishing Q1 of our roadmap is a big step, but we are not stopping here. We are already planning the next phase of improvements and features for the coming months. As always, we appreciate your feedback, so let us know what you think of these updates.
Thank you for your support, and we will see you on your next shift. Stay safe, and good luck surviving.
For a full breakdown of everything we've updated, you can check out the complete patch notes here.

notes.title: Hired 2 Die Gets Brazillian voice acting
notes.content:
The official Brazilian Portuguese voice-over is now available, bringing even more immersion to players. For the voice of the Announcer, we brought in the talented [b]Vanessa Angelo[/b], who did an outstanding job, and for the enigmatic Ringmaster, we secured a big name: [b]Carlinhos Silveira[/b], one of Brazil’s greatest voice actors.
 
If his name sounds familiar, it’s no coincidence. Carlinhos Silveira is the voice behind iconic characters such as [b]Shaka of Virgo[/b] (Saint Seiya: Knights of the Zodiac), [b]Gollum[/b] (The Lord of the Rings), [b]Oh Il-Nam[/b] (Squid Game), as well as [b]Zeff and Dr. Hogback[/b] (One Piece). Now, he brings all his expertise to make the Ringmaster an even more terrifying villain.
 
To celebrate this exciting news, during [b]Steam’s Spring Sale, Hired 2 Die will be 20% off[/b]. If you haven’t been hired by the Intersection yet, this is your chance to grab the game at a special price.

notes.content:
As we near the end of the development of Hired 2 Die, we’re thrilled to share some of the exciting final touches and polish we’re adding to the game. Let’s dive right in!
 
[h1]Traps and the Ringmaster’s Influence[/h1]
The Ringmaster has prepared the stage for his final act, introducing new stationary traps to his casino. Among these are exhaust vents, consumed by mold, which release poisonous gas in desperate bursts at anyone lingering beneath them.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/a1585d59379ec369d7e346f5d5c5631cf648a68d.gif[/img]
[i]Be mindful of the mold—breathe in too much, and…[/i]

[i] You’ll be snared in his strings forever![/i]

[h1]Cutscenes and Lore[/h1]

[i]Sometimes, the credits aren’t the end.[/i]

[i]Can’t you understand it’s perfection?[/i]
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/b031a2c055be67d8547ade3cbe567c2572065580.gif[/img]
[i]What’s that? Oh well, back to work… [/i]
 
[h1]Hunt Contracts[/h1]

We’ve finalized the balance for the “Hunt” contracts, making them the ultimate test of everything you’ve learned throughout the game. These missions push your skills, strategies, and perks to their limits, culminating in an explosive and satisfying payoff.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/926184c1eb74452f7799d1293d9bc2b10eea2d19.gif[/img]
[i]Let’s blow this damned place up.[/i]
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/26c4691c90694cb357e300fc3a623e5bd0c376bb.gif[/img]
[i]That was REALLY close.[/i]

[h1]A Big Thank You![/h1]

Our next devlog will be the final one before release and will focus on something every worker yearns for: achievements!

From the Electric Monkeys team, we wish you a Merry Christmas, happy holidays, and an amazing new year. With the release so close, it’s going to be a fantastic one for us!

[h2][b]PERKS AND LOBBY CUSTOMIZATION[/b][/h2]

Intersection has granted you the ability to purchase new anomalous furniture that empowers your character with unique abilities. These range from increased running speed to using cameras to help your friends and disable monsters.

notes.title: Devlog #013 | The House Always Wins
notes.content:
As a new year dawns, we're thrilled to update our community on the tremendous strides we've taken since our last Devlog. Let us present our latest endeavor:

[b][h2]"The House Always Wins."[/h2][/b]
Step into the the Grand Aethernus Casino, the domain of the cunning Ringmaster and his entourage. A street artist by trade and manipulator by necessity, the Ringmaster orchestrates daily shows with his troupe, luring patrons into the casino, skillfully fostering their indulgences to ensure they keep returning—or never leave at all.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/49acd48ff943fd72c5fd99e0dbffdabca4addce8.jpg[/img]

The Aethernus, once an old hotel, now stands transformed into a four-story casino complex. It comprises a basement, a stage for the Ringmaster's performances, a casino where “The Beast” incredible feats of strength entice gamblers, and a hotel section where the enigmatic "Magic Eye" captivates guests with enchanting tricks and vivid retellings of the troupe's greatest achievements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/9dfe1f46aa1bf7b0be770079a1f145788fc20cef.gif[/img]

Regrettably, all things come to an end. A series of vanishing acts culminated in the tragic murder of one troupe member, abruptly halting the shows and causing the Ringmaster to disappear. The enigmatic agency known as Intersection took a keen interest in the building, purchasing it and enlisting your services to uncover its concealed secrets.

Gather your friends and embark on the quest to unravel the mysteries of the Aethernus Casino. But be careful! The Ringmaster still haunts these halls, craving one final, spectacular performance—with you as the new unwitting members of the troupe. Your employers suspect that an eerie distortion within the casino has the power to manipulate perceptions, inducing hallucinations and subjecting individuals to the Ringmaster's control after prolonged exposure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/4baaa22c1742c539150fb101e5385da22033610a.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/221f98015f8fb58a332bc88ca1deaf08a6100e0a.jpg[/img]

There's an abundance of exciting features to reveal including new monsters, innovative mechanics, and forthcoming details about the release date. Stay tuned for our next devlogs. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/580e459db5feb9de6ac8927dd00625a7f999758e.gif[/img]

Thank you for reading, and here's to a fantastic new year ahead. Don't forget to take a look and wishlist our upcoming prologue!

notes.content:
Hello and welcome to our first Devlog of 2023. By the way things are going, there are only a few of these left before the game is released! Today we will take a look at a new contract available in the game: “A Simple Job”. This stage is set in an old factory building bought by a failing game studio called IQD. We don’t want to give too much of the story away, that’s for the player to figure it out! But what we can say is that this contract is composed by three different zones:

With their last remaining funds, they bought an old factory in an isolated area. Due to the rush to get their new project in development, they didn’t have the time to set-up an adequate workspace, so they removed the machines and put the office equipment wherever they would fit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/b042bb362658db99f727dd8cb68d7516f6f61e97.jpg[/img]

•	Server area / Old Warehouse: An expansive area where the servers were hastily put. A very claustrophobic area that forces the player to move between small spaces where creatures could be waiting to attack.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/ea07e8e890f75231bda7d483443d2d902397c665.jpg[/img]

•	Unfinished office: This area was in-construction while IQD final project was being made, but sadly, it was not to be. Due to the disappearance of the creative director the project was canceled, and the construction was never finished.

There are a lot of other interesting rooms, new puzzles and objectives, but we will leave those for you to find out. We may have exciting news in the following weeks, so keep tuned for more info!

notes.title: Devlog #008 | The elements of a job
notes.content:
[h2]The satisfaction of a job well-done![/h2]

Hey there folks! We are back with another Devlog. This month we will be showing you various new mechanics that complement the core of one of the themes of the game: pulling off an extraordinary job.

In Hired 2 Die the players are hired to observe, document and capture creatures for the shadowy “Intersection” agency. To avoid suspicion and civilian casualties a semblance of normalcy must be kept. So the areas affected by paranormal activity are closed under the pretense of being sold off or in need of serious repairs.

Therefore, it’s also the player’s job to execute cleaning, repairing, equipment installation and other various jobs. But these small jobs are not executed without reward! Everything done in the easier parts of the contract will be recorded by the game, making the final job of containing the creatures a lot easier.

Some examples of possible jobs and benefits are:
[list]
[*] Puddles: Stepping on them attract creatures. The player can clean any wet areas so that they won’t be a problem in higher difficulties.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/102b03998587e6bf78050228477223c2c243ea29.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Trash piles: Traversing them reduces the player velocity, making avoiding monsters harder. Like puddles, they can be cleaned permanently after being burned in the incinerator.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/8fc43ddcc2f57662d7e5c528243542a1bb380e86.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Blinds: Can be installed permanently and closed by the player to restrict the line of sight of hostile creatures. [/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/0b1241f530f17971572418a12d2fb5e34ecb4a35.gif[/img] 

[list]
[*] Doors: After installed, can be opened/closed to help in chases.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/94be097faf4d55026b328141545cbfc1333de995.gif[/img]

There are other jobs that can be done, but we will keep then a secret from now. Here is an example of an area after all jobs are done:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/77d014a20203baca25450936bb679311b2d47a6f.png[/img]

With all these new tasks it was necessary to make traversing the level carrying more stuff faster, so we added a cart that can move various objects at once.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/c38b0cc0df066de8de9992ca0dabc21d05255540.gif[/img]

However, using the cart restricts your vision, making chases more tense and harder.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/8cdc37eaad033ea5f78aadd0bd1c4a7c98918e08.gif[/img]

There are other systems that are also shared between levels of the same contract, but we will be talking about that next month!

notes.title: Devlog #007 | How things change!
notes.content:
Hey there! My name is Vinicyus, I am the lead game designer of Hired 2 Die. Today I would like to talk about what we have been working on.

It's been a pretty busy month, hence the delay in Devlogs. So, to compensate for the wait, in this Devlog we would like to show you various changes we made since our last post.
When we last talked it was about the tutorial, so it’s only appropriate that we begin by discussing it. We felt that the old tutorial was not up to par graphically with the rest of the game. Instead of only adjusting the textures, we have opted instead of redesigning the whole scene. Here are our results so far:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/a9fc9e44865fcef62a10962177486cb07862a383.jpg[/img]
 
 
Speaking of subpar graphics, we redid all the lighting in the project. We weren’t happy how players could easily navigate without any light sources. Now, navigating without a flashlight or turning the lights on will be a lot harder. Besides, the game looks a lot better now!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/d8f2f3c659f246e65ff0b72a1470af0f4b7800a5.jpg[/img]

Another problem that we tackled these last weeks was how similar both our monsters look. Even though they behave very differently from one another, we felt that they looked too similar and were hard to discern. So, we redesigned the second twin to have a different silhouette and better fit his design concept, we hope you all like his new look!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/468f3d487c6226625f8973c53cd13200e18cf899.jpg[/img]

On the gameplay front we improved the behavior of both Twins, making then harder to avoid and also act smarter. Various adjustments were made to systems that were not being used very often. One example is the radius that the alarms; previously they were too small to be useful. After various tests, we improved the system to consider walls and doors and attract the creatures more often.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/49de63c4792558701f072aa263669de9ea98e421.jpg[/img]
 
Finally, there are various small fixes and new additions: a new interface for the security system, new player models, anomalies, concept art and so on.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/e2131b3293d20b2fad3f0ba66cc31eac93d9ec1e.jpg[/img]

As you can see, we have been very busy these last few weeks. Since we are now implementing new stages so we can finish a playable demo, we have decided to make the Devlogs monthly, that way we can focus more on the development of the game and still keep you guys informed. 

That’s what we got this month! Thanks for your patience, keep tuned for all our new progress reports.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/18863dcaf26c6fb3c4f7a37e68aff1f0d1f50b8a.gif[/img]

notes.title: Devlog #006 | Tutorial
notes.content:
Hi, it's been a while since our last devlog (sorry about that). Releasing a game (even in the alpha stage) is difficult. It leaves us with a lot of things to fix and organize. In the last couple of weeks, we focused on tackling these problems, so the new features can be created smoothly.

Hired 2 Die is not the type of game you figure out what's happening and what you need to do intuitively. There are two things we thought we could improve in the game: clarity and story.

Before starting the closed alpha playtest, we noticed some people were having problems understanding the objectives, how-to's, and why the hell someone would work in a place with vicious creatures on the loose. So instead of creating floating arrows pointing to objectives, and on-screen text, we decided to design a tutorial with the basic situations of a job. It also gives the player a sense of what's going on. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/4667e60f54835d3720c8c2acf2c1e872d3483756.png[/img]

To make things easier to understand, we put the player in the company's headquarters to start the "new worker's training." The player must perform basic tasks and fix incidents that might happen during the run, like energy shortage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/8e3178522406fa9c771732d5ea852d4f7ed4c4f8.png[/img]

After the tests, we noticed small tasks are much more valuable than we thought, so we are currently designing more tasks for the player to do while designing new puzzles with interesting challenges.

notes.title: Devlog #004 | Singleplayer Mode
notes.content:
Hello guys,

First of all, I would like to apologize for the delay in posting the devlog. It should be posted last week, during the Steam Survival Festival. 

I believe I've already said it before, but during the last few weeks, the team has been preparing the game for our closed alpha. We created our [url=https://hired2die.com/]website[/url] and added a form so anyone can request a free key. We send it by e-mail, individually.

Now, with the closed alpha getting closer, you might be one of those players wondering: [i]I prefer to play alone, but the game seems to be designed for 2 players. Are the developers considering the singleplayer option?[/i]

Yes, we are! The basic principle of playing with a friend is the exchange of information. Usually, what happens is that one player stays in the security room watching CCTV cameras, collecting information, buying items, etc. And the other player is adventuring in dark corridors, doing the actual job, but also giving information about the system to the first player.

Now, when playing alone, it would be too hard to be in two places at the same time, travelling between two different rooms to check if the cable should go on the left or right plug is not exactly convenient. So, we gave the player the best gift ever, this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/780633794a1819e6147ee50df1ca58d09208679b.png[/img]

[h2]The intersection companion[/h2]
The intersection companion is a tablet designed to give you access to all the information you need. It does not count as an item, so it won't occupy a slot in your inventory and prevent you from getting the items you might need.

The tablet has functionality from both computers. You can access the CCTV Cameras, use the same supported features of the main computer, and buy items on the go. There are two different views when using the tablet:
[list]
[*] Focus Mode - it's a fullscreen view, just like the ones on the PC, for you to focus on the information.
[*] Preview Mode - the character holds it in front of you, taking about 1/4 of the screen. It's useful to walk around while still checking for creatures. You can even hold an item in the other hand.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/99eddc5387972d4f0b28e0ee2f2cb24cd787f2b7.gif[/img]

We are still exploring possibilities with the tablet, like navigation and actions through shortcuts, so you don't need to focus on it every time. The Intersection Companion is a powerful tool. We must be careful to keep things balanced and fun to play. That's why it is not available when playing with a friend.

notes.title: Devlog #002 | The Store
notes.content:
Welcome back! I am Hugo Campos, responsible for the development of Hired 2 Die. In "Devlog #001 | What do I do in Hired 2 Die?" you learned about H2D and its main objectives. This time, I will present to you the Store, how it works, and why it is vital in all matches. If you didn't see the last Devlog, check it out:

https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1729140/view/4868968718724400141
[h1]I'm poor, what now?[/h1]

As we explained before, in your first match, you will probably choose an easier contract, i.e. one that has [b]Ordinary Tasks[/b]. In that case, these tasks won't require items from the Store, you will be able to complete the match with good coordination and planning. But, imagine the following situation: during a match, you see yourself without money, but you need to buy an item from the Store to complete the contract objective. What to do now? 

[h2]Earning money with Anomalies[/h2]

Anomalies are unnatural changes to random objects in the setting, the mere existence of supernatural creatures causes anomalies. These Anomalies are very important to the research team at Intersection (the company that hires people to do these "wonderful" tasks), for that reason, each player receives a photographic camera specially designed to deal with these Anomalies. 

This camera has advanced components of cutting-edge technology, and for that reason, you can see things through this camera that our eyes can't see. Using this camera will make you able to visualize where the Anomalies are in the environment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/5c7e6018f4010921507365785f2522a413bfa867.png[/img]

After photographing an Anomaly, it ceases to exist, the only evidence remaining is the photography itself. This photo will immediately be sent as a piece of evidence, and payment will be made to you accordingly with the Anomaly rarity. You can keep doing this until the last Anomaly is fixed, that is if you can find it.

[previewyoutube=UxfOo3WqxPQ;full][/previewyoutube] 

From the point of view of development, Anomalies are very fun to create, currently, they involve changing a characteristic of an object: increasing or decreasing its size, making it shake, or even changing the texture of portraits. Some anomalies are simply objects that shouldn't be there, things completely out of context. In the future, we intend to create more bizarre and funny Anomalies, if you have any interesting ideas we have a [url=https://discord.com/invite/a46g4s9j59]Discord[/url] channel called "[b]#suggestions[/b]" that you can use to, well, send suggestions.

[h2]Contract Items x Utility Items?[/h2]

There are two types of items to buy in the store: contract items and utility items. As mentioned in the last Devlog, in advanced contracts, the players must fix some kind of system. In that case, these systems have missing parts and the players must buy these parts in the Store. Therefore, many times it is impossible to complete a contract without using the Store.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/4e789dc364454f1be092b53525f0ab619f832f73.png[/img]

On the other hand, you can buy utility items for yourself, these items may help you to complete your objectives and deal with obstacles. For example:
[list] 
[*] [b]Plier[/b] – The plier is useful to break chains that lock certain doors and openings. In some cases, the chain is locked with a padlock, and you must find a way to open the padlock. But if you don't have time for this but have money, you can buy the plier to cut the chain.
[*][b]Strong Flashlight[/b] – Some creatures are affected by light, but the default flashlight is not strong enough for that, buying a strong light will give you a way to defend yourself.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/12f88915b34c356763a96f2deaf1baa393e5886d.png[/img]

[h2]Delivery[/h2]

At last, we arrived at the final step of buying an item: the delivery. In Hired 2 Die, the items sold are delivered after a period, simulating real-life. This period may vary based on random factors of the Store, it can last some hours (the game time equivalent to minutes) or days of work, which makes you lose a day of its deadline to complete the job. Optionally, you can pay a higher value to make the item arrive immediately. The items are delivered in the lockers located in the main room or in the storeroom.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/5bda9c17b1e49adf440270a42955a9b34ad2c83d.png[/img]

I hope you already have a good idea of how to play [b]Hired 2 Die[/b]. If you are interested and wish to buy the game, don't forget to add it to your wishlist so you don't miss its launch:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1729140/Hired_2_Die/

notes.title: Devlog #001 | What do I do in Hired 2 Die?
notes.content:
Hello again, my name is Hugo and as promised in the last post, we'll keep reporting the development of Hired 2 Die every 2 weeks, if you know nothing about H2D, I recommend reading the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1729140/view/3352380820056809385]Devlog #000[/url].

Sometimes when there is a new horror game, I feel that I've already seen that game before, until I understand what makes that game unique. Right now, you might be associating Hired 2 Die with other horror games. To clarify what makes H2D unique, we listed here its main rules and objectives.

[h1]Walkthrough[/h1]
In H2D the players work for a company called [b][i]Intersection[/i][/b]. Before starting a new match the players must select a work contract, that will define what is the main objective of that match. There are 3 types of contracts in the game: Ordinary Tasks, Complex Tasks, and Hunting Tasks.

[h2]Planning Phase[/h2]
Each match involves different maps, items, strategies, and deadlines, for that reason at the beginning of the match the players have the opportunity to plan their steps in the main room, where they will organize items, access security footage, and buy auxiliary items to help them out.

[h2]Ordinary Tasks[/h2]
These tasks won't involve much mental effort to be solved. Usually, it will require some type of manual work like carrying objects to the correct places or cleaning dirty rooms. They are low-risk and low-reward contracts, a good start for beginners.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/9cc2df4a075abb324cb78a182a65c0e0ecf7583f.png[/img]

[h2]Complex Tasks[/h2]
The players need to execute a complex procedure to complete this objective. The complex tasks always involve fixing some non-intuitive system that is presented to the players in a puzzle format. To increase the replayability value of the game, the solution of each module of this puzzle is randomly generated, this way even if the player completes the objective, it will be different in another match.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/d9f80913d90a8546d900f546259575a7099e4451.png[/img]

Try and error won't be a good way to fix the system, some vital information about the solution is written in a manual, and it can be accessed on the main room's computer. Thus, making it essential to have clear communication between the players.

The player that assumes the guide's role, shall conduct the other player to the desired place avoiding "unpleasant surprises" along the way. The security systems will help in this task, he can live access security camera footage, open/close doors, turn lights on/off, and access the information in the manual to solve the puzzle. Though getting distracted here might be fatal since he might not be alone in the main room.

The player that will risk his life in the dark corridors, should carry with him items to solve the puzzle and to protect himself from panic situations. Besides moving with intelligence to avoid stumbling with a creature. This player also needs to communicate clearly, since each system has different brands and characteristics. These differences are crucial to the guide in order to find the correct solution to the puzzle.

[h2]Hunting Tasks[/h2]
We are still working on many things about the hunting tasks. So we won't show much in detail. Now, if you are the kind of player that is tired of being hunted, this task will allow you to assume the role of the hunter. 

In order to hunt a creature, you must become the creature, understand its behavior, and how to manipulate and deceive it. To find out all the information about a creature you can count on a special camera provided to you for free by [b][i]Intersection[/i][/b], with this camera you should take a picture of the creature specific behavior and send it back to [b][i]Intersection[/i][/b]. You will receive an analysis of the creature explaining its behavior, this will give you hints on how to face these creatures.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/ab378aa10e4a6da2634e0a3323ee5e20dc40a688.png[/img]

[h2]Conclusion of the Contract[/h2]
To end the contract, the players must clock out and leave using the elevator, but the salary paid by its conclusion depends on some factors:
[olist]
[*] You need to be alive. Even though it is possible to end a contract with a deceived colleague, this won't be very good for your salary.
[*] Death. Obviously, when all the players die the contract ends, but since there is nobody alive to receive the salary, they might pay the firewood to cremate your body.
[*] Deadline: the deadline is measured in days. You can try to solve everything in a single day, but there is an ideal time to stay in a game, after a certain number of hours, the creatures get too aggressive. Besides that, they naturally become more aggressive as the days go by.
[/olist]

In the next Devlogs, we will explain more about what to do with the money you earned. And just to remind you, if you have any questions or are interested in talking to us, you can join us on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/a46G4S9J59]Discord Channel[/url].

notes.title: Devlog #000 | Welcome to Hired 2 Die
notes.content:
Welcome! If you are reading this post, it means you are probably interested in our game, and that means a lot to us! I'm Hugo Campos, the Co-Founder of Electric Monkeys Studio. If you don’t know us, we have developed [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1020310/Gravity_Heroes/]Gravity Heroes[/url] (that just won the “Golden Cube” award yesterday, crazy right?!), a local multiplayer game for up to four players and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1392690/Gravitational/]Gravitational[/url], a VR game that received several awards at BIG Festival and SBGames. However, we are not here to talk about past projects, we want to talk about our new game: Hired 2 Die. 
 
[b]What is Hired 2 Die? [/b]
 
Hired 2 Die is a game focused on the cooperation between two players. You and a friend are the new employees in an organization that deals with the paranormal, offering contracts that pay a salary based on the difficulty of the tasks in its clauses. You will have to move boxes around an office or even fix slot machines in a casino, all this while trying to survive the ploys of terrible creatures. Only through teamwork will you be able to finish your job in time. And, if you are feeling courageous (and lucky!), you can even accept a contract to try and imprison the creatures. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/20d4c470686369e060381dec643e9dabd6603d86.png[/img]
  
This Devlog #0 is the first part of a new vision for the project. We are committing to better our communication process with our community, and the first step towards this objective is in the creation of Devlogs, which will be updated every two weeks showing our plans, different game strategies, new mechanics and the development process of new monsters, all in a manner which is as clear and transparent as possible. 
 
[b]What are we doing now? [/b]
  
We are hard at work to finalize the development of the first stage of the game, the office. This milestone represents something very important for us: a playable alpha version. A stage in Hired 2 Die has three maps (every one representing a different difficulty level), three advanced tasks, some basic tasks, and, obviously, monsters, for a unique, strategic, and fun experience. 
 
[b]What is already in the game? [/b]
	 
	We have added various tools to help you prevail and finish your job with perfection. First, you have access to the powerful security systems present at your job site. You can turn lights on or off, open and close doors, and trigger alarms remotely. But your most important tool is the security cameras, which let you see rooms and corridors from a “safe” location, keeping you ahead of terrible creatures lurking in the shadows, tracking their position, restricting their movements, distracting them with alarms, and controlling the lights to keep them away from your objectives. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41320579/4e38369dc3732c41d476ed6a8dd34f6be45e85bf.jpg[/img]

	Second, you can manipulate various equipment and items, that can be delivered during the stage to help you formulate the perfect plan to execute your job. However, everything in life has a price, be it money or time. The items bought during the stage must be paid for with the money received from completing tasks, and, unless you pay extra, the delivery man might take a while to bring your orders. Therefore, buying items must be carefully planned between the players, since, as the days go by, the horrors that inhabit your workplace get more menacing and dangerous. 

	Last but certainly not least, the biggest of your aces: your partner! You can monitor the various security cameras, making use of the doors, alarms, and other systems to distract or restrict enemies, while your friend desperately tries to finish a job, that, sometimes, needs calm and attention.
